paper.title: Humanoid Manipulation Interface: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Robot-Free Demonstrations

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Direct humanoid loco-manipulation data-collection and whole-body-policy study.

sections_read.purpose: Identify the robot-operation bottleneck in whole-body data collection.
Inspect robot-free tracking and manipulation-centric control.

research_question: Can robot-free full-body demonstration collection improve humanoid loco-manipulation data throughput without sacrificing feasibility?
contributions: A robot-free full-body capture workflow with human-in-the-loop IK preview and a compatible hierarchical policy interface.

method.summary: Wearable trackers capture human motion; a previewed IK mapping checks humanoid feasibility, while a high-level diffusion policy commands a manipulation-centric whole-body controller.
assumptions: Wearable trackers remain observable under suitable lighting and texture.
A platform-specific low-level whole-body controller is available.

study_context.sample_or_scale: 350 demonstrations; a 15-minute throughput comparison; seven environments and seven bottles for generalization studies.

evaluation.design: Capability, generalization and collection-efficiency studies compare HuMI with TWIST2 and evaluate trained policies on the real robot.

findings.finding: Robot-free collection roughly doubled raw episode throughput and increased acceptance in the timed comparison.
findings.scope: One 15-minute operator comparison on the reported capture systems.

author_stated.limitation: Tracking depends on texture and lighting, low-level controllers are not yet general, and evaluation uses one robot platform.

reader_inferred.boundary: Collection efficiency does not by itself establish autonomous policy generalization.
reader_inferred.basis: The throughput experiment measures accepted demonstrations, while downstream studies remain task- and platform-specific.

transfer_boundary: Useful where human full-body motion is a suitable task prior and a compatible low-level controller can execute retargeted commands.

design_strengths: Measures both collection throughput and downstream real-robot behavior.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Both systems are compared over the same wall-clock collection period, though ergonomics and operator familiarity may differ.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Acceptance rate and acceptable-episode time directly capture data-collection productivity.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Hardware and protocols are documented in appendices.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Single platform and capture setup limit broad transfer claims.

evidence_cards.claim: In a 15-minute comparison, HuMI collected 62 episodes versus 28 for TWIST2, with 96.7% versus 64.3% acceptance; time per acceptable episode fell to 30.0% of TWIST2.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports robot-free capture as a way to scale feasible whole-body demonstrations.
evidence_cards.summary: The timed comparison jointly reports quantity, quality and accepted-data cost.
evidence_cards.source_context: HuMI yields substantially higher throughput, collecting 62 episodes versus 28 with TWIST2, while also achieving a higher acceptance rate ( 96.7% vs. 64.3% ). HuMI’s streamlined, robot-free workflow further reduces the average time per acceptable episode to 30.0% of that of TWIST2

verification.rationale: The result paragraph contains all three comparisons and the two systems.
